title: Investigation of cognitive performance and neurometabolic changes using 31P-MRS and 1H-MRS in women during menstruation while on a creatine diet
summary: The aim of the study is to investigate changes in cerebral metabolic parameters and cognitive performance in women during menstruation. Furthermore, the study aims to examine whether a daily creatine intake of 15 g affects these changes during the menstrual period.
conditions: Investigation of the influence of the menstrual cycle on brain metabolism, cognitive performance, and blood levels of estrogen and creatine in women.

interventions.name: Two-week daily oral supplementation of 15 g/day, followed by a two-week maintenance phase of 8 g/day of the dietary supplement creatine monohydrate following a baseline measurement. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
•       at least 18 years old
•	Availability of a written declaration of consent
Exclusion criteria:
•	over 40 years of age and in menopause
•	any medication affecting the study parameters, particularly centrally acting drugs and substances
•	kidney disease, renal insufficiency, diabetes, or any indication of impaired renal function
•	intake of substances in cumulative amounts hazardous to the kidneys (e.g., a lifetime total of 1 kg of ibuprofen)
•	intake of more than 30 g of creatine supplements in the 6 months prior to measurement
•	intake of any creatine supplements in the 3 weeks prior to measurement
•	epilepsy, or one or more seizures occurring after the age of 12
•	diabetes
•	drug dependence, smoking
•	any other condition that, in the opinion of the attending physicians, renders the subject unsuitable (e.g., claustrophobia)
•	electrical implants for stimulation, diagnosis, or therapy (e.g., pacemakers, infusion pumps)
•	Tattoos on the head and neck.
•	dental metal causing severe artifacts (potential exclusion following the preliminary scan)
•	any other metallic objects on or in the body (e.g., joint implants, surgical screws, etc.), except those confirmed beforehand to be MR-safe
•	intensive grinding work on metallic objects within the past month
•	physical complaints (e.g., back pain) that make lying still for an extended period difficult
•	severe obesity or large body circumference (the scanner's inner diameter is 60 cm)
•	pregnancy
•	current use of hormonal contraception (e.g., oral contraceptives, hormonal IUD, vaginal ring, or depot injection) or use thereof within the three months prior to the start of the study.
